This citation covers the preceding paragraph. ==== {{IPA|/h/}} ==== At an archaic stage, the realizations of {{IPA|/h/}} (from Latin {{IPA|/f/}}) would have been approximately as follows:{{Harvcoltxt|Lloyd|1987|pp=214–215}}; {{Harvcoltxt|Penny|2002|p=92}} * {{IPA|[ɸ]}} before {{IPA|[i e a]}} or {{IPA|[j ɾ l]}} * {{IPA|[h]}}{{efn|developed from older {{IPA|[ɸ]}} via dissimilation before rounded vowels}} before {{IPA|[o]}} or {{IPA|[u]}} * {{IPA|[ʍ]}} or {{IPA|[hɸ]}} before {{IPA|[w]}} By early Old Spanish, {{IPA|[ɸ]}} had been replaced with {{IPA|[h]}} before all vowels{{Harvcoltxt|Penny|2002|p=92}} and possibly before {{IPA|[j]}} as well.{{Harvcoltxt|Lloyd|1987|pp=215–216, 322–323}} In later Old Spanish, surviving {{IPA|[ɸ]}} and {{IPA|[ʍ]}}/{{IPA|[hɸ]}} were modified to {{IPA|[f]}} in urban speech, likely due to the influx of numerous [[French language|French]] and [[Occitan language|Occitan]] speakers (and their particular pronunciation of Latin) beginning in the twelfth century.{{Harvcoltxt|Penny|2002|p=92}}; {{Harvcoltxt|Lloyd|1987|p=324}} Various words with {{IPA|[f]}} were then borrowed into Spanish, leading to [[Minimal pair|minimal pairs]] like {{IPA|[ˈfoɾma]}} “form” (a borrowing) and {{IPA|[ˈhoɾma]}} “shoemaker's last” (inherited from Latin {{lang|la|forma}}). It was also sometimes written in [[Arabic script]] in a practice called [[Aljamiado|Aljamía]]. === {{IPA|/ɲ ʎ/}} === These sounds were spelt {{angbr|nn}} and {{angbr|ll}} respectively.{{efn|Continuing the spellings of Latin /nn/ and /ll/, which were [[Palatalization_in_the_Romance_languages#/ll_nn/_and_initial_/l_n/|in many cases]] the origin of Old Spanish /ɲ/ and /ʎ/.}} {{angbr|nn}} was often [[Scribal abbreviation|abbreviated]] to {{angbr|ñ}}, which went on to become the normal spelling of {{IPA|/ɲ/}} in Modern Spanish. ==== Graeco-Latin diagraphs ==== Old Spanish featured the digraphs {{angbr|ch}}, {{angbr|ph}}, {{angbr|(r)rh}}, and {{angbr|th}} which were simplified to {{angbr|c}}, {{angbr|f}}, {{angbr|(r)r}}, {{angbr|t}} in Modern Spanish. Examples include: * {{lang|osp|christiano}} (modern {{lang|es|cristiano}}) * {{lang|osp|triumpho}} (modern {{lang|es|triunfo}}) * {{lang|osp|myrrha}} (modern {{lang|es|mirra}}) * {{lang|osp|theatro}} (modern {{lang|es|teatro}}) ==== ⟨y⟩ ==== {{angbr|y}} often stood for {{IPA|/i/}} in word-initial position. In this context it has since been respelt to {{angbr|i}} in Modern Spanish. ==== Sibilants ==== (The following table does not account for [[sandhi]] contexts.) {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: center;" |+{{Citation needed|date=September 2024}} ! scope="col" | consonant ! scope="col" | spelling ! scope="col" | context |- | rowspan="4" | {{IPAslink|t͡s}} |{{angle bracket|ç}} | any |- |{{angle bracket|c}} |before {{angle bracket|e}} or {{angle bracket|i}} |- | rowspan="5" |{{angle bracket|z}} |final |- |before a voiceless consonant |- | rowspan="3" | {{IPAslink|d͡z}} | before a voiced consonant |- |initial |- |intervocalic |- | rowspan="3" |{{IPAslink|s}} |{{angle bracket|ss}} |intervocalic |- | rowspan="4" |{{angle bracket|s}} |initial |- |before a voiceless consonant |- | rowspan="2" |{{IPAslink|z}} |before a voiced consonant |- |intervocalic |- | rowspan="2" |{{IPAslink|ʃ}} |{{angle bracket|x}} |any |- | rowspan="2" |{{angle bracket|i}}{{efn|⟨j⟩ in modernized spelling}} |final |- | rowspan="2" |{{IPAslink|ʒ}} |before a vowel |- |{{angle bracket|g}} |before {{angle bracket|e}} or {{angle bracket|i}} |- |{{IPAslink|t͡ʃ}} |{{angle bracket|ch}} |any |} ==Morphology== In Old Spanish, [[perfect (grammar)|perfect]] constructions of movement verbs, such as {{lang|osp|ir}} ('(to) go') and {{lang|osp|venir}} ('(to) come'), were formed using the auxiliary verb {{lang|osp|ser}} ('(to) be'), as in Italian and French: {{lang|osp|Las mugieres '''son llegadas''' a Castiella}} was used instead of {{lang|es|Las mujeres han llegado a Castilla}} ('The women have arrived in Castile'). Possession was expressed with the verb {{lang|osp|aver}} (Modern Spanish {{lang|es|haber}}, '(to) have'), rather than {{lang|osp|tener}}: {{lang|osp|Pedro ha dos fijas}} was used instead of {{lang|es|Pedro tiene dos hijas}} ('Pedro has two daughters'). In the [[Perfect (grammar)|perfect]] tenses, the [[past participle]] often agreed with the [[grammatical gender|gender]] and [[grammatical number|number]] of the [[object (grammar)#Types|direct object]]: {{lang|osp|María '''ha cantadas''' dos canciones}} was used instead of Modern Spanish {{lang|es|María ha cantado dos canciones}} ('María has sung two songs'). However, that was inconsistent even in the earliest texts. The prospective aspect was formed with the verb {{lang|osp|ir}} ('(to) go') along with the verb in infinitive, with the difference that Modern Spanish includes the preposition {{lang|es|a}}: :{{lang|osp|Al Çid beso la mano, la senna '''ua''' tomar.}} (''[[Cantar de mio Cid]]'', 691) :{{lang|es|Al Cid besó la mano, la enseña '''va a''' tomar.}} (Modern Spanish equivalent) [[Personal pronoun]]s and [[substantive]]s were placed after the verb in any tense or [[grammatical mood|mood]] unless a stressed word was before the verb.{{examples|date=January 2016}} The future and the conditional tenses were not yet fully [[grammaticalization|grammaticalised]] as inflections; rather, they were still periphrastic formations of the verb {{lang|osp|aver}} in the present or imperfect indicative followed by the infinitive of a main verb.{{Harvcoltxt|Penny|2002|p=210}} Pronouns, therefore, by the general placement rules, could be inserted between the main verb and the auxiliary in these periphrastic tenses, as still occurs with [[Portuguese language|Portuguese]] ([[mesoclisis]]): : {{lang|osp|E dixo: ― Tornar-'''m'''-é a Jherusalem.}} (''[[Fazienda de Ultra Mar]]'', 194) : {{lang|es|Y dijo: ― '''Me''' tornaré a Jerusalén.}} (literal translation into Modern Spanish) : {{lang|pt|E disse: ― Tornar-'''me'''-ei a Jerusalém.}} (literal translation into Portuguese) : And he said: "I will return to Jerusalem." (English translation) : {{lang|osp|En pennar '''gelo''' he por lo que fuere guisado}} (''[[Cantar de mio Cid]]'', 92) : {{lang|es|'''Se lo''' empeñaré por lo que fuere razonable}} (literal translation into Modern Spanish) : {{lang|pt|Penhorar-'''lho'''-ei pelo que for razoável}} (literal Modern Portuguese equivalent) : I will pawn '''them it''' for whatever it be reasonable (English translation) When there was a stressed word before the verb, the pronouns would go before the verb: {{lang|osp|non '''gelo''' empeñar he por lo que fuere guisado}}. Generally, an unstressed pronoun and a verb in [[simple sentence]]s combined into one word.{{Clarify|date=July 2011}} In a [[compound sentence (linguistics)|compound sentence]], the pronoun was found in the beginning of the [[dependent clause|clause]]: {{lang|osp|la manol va besar}} = {{lang|es|la mano le va a besar}}.{{Citation needed|date=July 2011}} The [[future subjunctive]] was in common use ({{lang|osp|fuere}} in the second example above) but it is generally now found only in legal or solemn discourse and in the spoken language in some dialects, particularly in areas of [[Venezuela]], to replace the imperfect subjunctive.Diccionario de dudas y dificultades de la lengua española. [[Manuel Seco|Seco, Manuel]]. Espasa-Calpe. 2002. Pp. 222–3. It was used similarly to its Modern Portuguese counterpart, in place of the modern present subjunctive in a subordinate clause after {{lang|es|si}}, {{lang|es|cuando}} etc., when an event in the future is referenced: : {{lang|osp|Si vos assi lo '''fizieredes''' e la ventura me '''fuere''' complida}} : {{lang|osp|Mando al vuestro altar buenas donas e ricas}} (''Cantar de mio Cid'', 223–224) : {{lang|es|Si vosotros así lo '''hiciereis''' y la ventura me '''fuere''' cumplida,}} : {{lang|es|Mando a vuestro altar ofrendas buenas y ricas}} (Modern Spanish equivalent) : {{lang|pt|Se vós assim o '''fizerdes''' e a ventura me '''for''' cumprida,}} : {{lang|pt|Mando a vosso altar oferendas boas e ricas.}} (Portuguese equivalent.) : If you do so and fortune is favourable toward me, : I will send to your altar fine and rich offerings (English translation) ==Vocabulary== {| align=center | class="wikitable plainrowheaders" !
